meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you (informal)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Не знаю, помнишь ты или нет.
examples.trans: I do not know whether you remember or not.
You are fired.
You are fired!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'wanted', paired with 'захотеть'.

examples.trans: Did you want to see me?

examples.text: Но я хотел поговорить про твою маму.
examples.trans: But I wanted to talk about your mom.
I want coffee.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'me', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: And you end up with six people.

examples.text: Вы у нас директор ресторана, Илья.
examples.trans: You are our restaurant director, Ilya.
And Dmitry Vladimirovich's tailcoat.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to see', paired with 'увидеть'.

examples.trans: Did you want to see me?
Hello, glad to see you.
How glad I am to see you!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'yes', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Yes, alright.
Let's go through the wedding script.
Make it faster, okay?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'адиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'sit down', paired with 'сесть'.

examples.trans: Sit down, please.
Sit down and hold the door.

examples.text: Садитесь и держите дверь. Никто не войдёт.
examples.trans: Sit down and hold the door. Nobody will come in.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пасибо'). Common neuter noun meaning 'thank you' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Thank you, Eleonora Andreyevna.
Thank you, I will stand.
Oh my goodness, thank you so much!

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'стоять'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will stand', paired with 'стоять'.

examples.text: И у вас будет всего два постоянных гостя.
examples.trans: And you will have only two regular guests.
Wait, don't go!
I'll stand here for a bit.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'нимать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'understand', paired with 'понять'.

examples.text: Катя, я понимаю, ты обижена на меня.
examples.trans: Katya, I understand you are upset with me.

examples.text: Я тебя понимаю, потому что я люблю тебя.
examples.trans: I understand you, because I love you.

examples.text: Я понимаю, что сейчас не вовремя.
examples.trans: I understand that now is not the right time.

meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'иженный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('offended / hurt').

examples.text: Шеф говорит, что это очень обиженный выбор.
examples.trans: The chef says that this is a very offended choice.

examples.text: У нас сегодня просто обиженный день в ресторане.
examples.trans: We are having a simply offended day at the restaurant today.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'on, onto', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: За нашим столиком будет сидеть олигарх.
examples.trans: An oligarch will be sitting at our table.

examples.text: Подождите, у нас столик на четверых.
examples.trans: Wait, our table is for four.

examples.text: Вы у нас директор ресторана, Илья.
examples.trans: You are our restaurant director, Ilya.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: It is for my niece.
This is very important to me.

examples.text: И Дима для меня последний вагон.
examples.trans: And Dima is the last train car for me.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, it (is)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: You tell me how to do it.

examples.text: И я хочу, чтобы повара испекли это печенье.
examples.trans: And I want the chefs to bake these cookies.

examples.text: Я читал сам про это дело.
examples.trans: I read about this matter myself.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'very', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Today is a very important banquet.
In short, what do you need?

examples.text: Свободного времени у тебя появится очень много.
examples.trans: You will suddenly have plenty of free time.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('important, mattering').

examples.trans: Today is a very important banquet.
This is very important to me.
It's an important question.

meanings.note: Prefix 'из-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'винить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'sorry', paired with 'извинять'.

examples.trans: Eleonora Andreyevna, sorry to interrupt.

examples.text: Извините, можно у вас автограф взять?
examples.trans: Excuse me, may I get your autograph?
Sorry, I cannot, there is a lot of work.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: You tell me how to do it.
Take it to my suite.

examples.text: Я надеюсь, вам повторять не надо.
examples.trans: I hope I do not need to repeat to you.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'can, am able to', paired with 'смочь'.

examples.trans: I can't today.
That can't be.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Свободного времени у тебя появится очень много.
examples.trans: You will suddenly have plenty of free time.
Sorry, I cannot, there is a lot of work.
Oh my goodness, thank you so much!

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'job, work' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Chef, everyone back to work.
Everyone get to work!

examples.text: Работать надо, а не моему мужу улыбаться.
examples.trans: You need to work, not smile at my husband.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: They called and will definitely come.

Take it to my suite.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to give', paired with 'давать'.

examples.text: Но я могу дать тебе выходной.
examples.trans: But I can give you a day off.

examples.text: Мы ведь в ЗАГС так можем опоздать.
examples.trans: We might be late to the registry office like this.
They might give us a star.

meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'ходной'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('day off').

examples.text: Но я могу дать тебе выходной.
examples.trans: But I can give you a day off.
It's a day off, after all.

examples.text: Что ты делаешь в эти выходные?
examples.trans: What are you doing this weekend?

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('guilty, at fault').

examples.text: Я виновата, я вмешивалась в твою жизнь.
examples.trans: I am at fault, I interfered in your life.
The marriage fell apart—the mother-in-law is to blame.
It's your fault!

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'interfered', paired with 'вмешаться'.

examples.trans: And you, stay out of it.

examples.text: Подарки надо ценить! А вы не вмешивайтесь.
examples.trans: You must appreciate gifts! And you, stay out of it.

examples.trans: I like coffee.
